BiblicalUsage: mârêʼ is master, the Aramaic word for lord, and it belongs to Daniel's court. In Daniel 2:47 Nebuchadnezzar calls Daniel's God a God of gods and a Lord of kings, and in Daniel 4:19 Daniel answers his lord the king with troubled thoughts. In Daniel 4:24 the decree of the Most High has come upon my lord the king, and in Daniel 5:23 Belshazzar lifts himself against the Lord of heaven. The word is the title men give kings, and the title that belongs to God.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe mârêʼ teaches me that earthly masters are many but the Lord of heaven is one. I hold that Daniel's God is the master worth serving.
